title: Closing time
summary: Closing Time is the 1973 debut album by Tom Waits, a set of ballads and barroom songs in the style of the late-night lounge singer. The lyrics are sung in the persona of a rambling, wistful narrator who sings about bars, lonely drives, lost love, and small-town characters. Songs in the record include "Ol' 55", "I Hope That I Don't Fall in Love with You", "Virginia Avenue", "Martha", and "Rosie". The text provided also contains later Waits material that was gathered alongside the album's lyrics: the instrumental and lyric sheets of the 1985 Rain Dogs album, including "Singapore", "Cemetery Polka", "Big Black Mariah", and "Jockey Full of Bourbon"; the Blue Valentines pieces "Small Change", "Red Shoes by the Drugstore", "Christmas Card from a Hooker in Minneapolis", and "Romeo Is Bleeding"; "Way Down in the Hole"; and songs from the 1991 film soundtrack Night on Earth, such as "Good Old World" and "The Other Side of the World". The collection is a songbook-style compilation of lyrics rather than a continuous narrative, and it spans several decades of Waits's writing.
